title: Fewer things and room for yourselves

captions.energy: Clinging to material proof of security

meaning: Domestic comfort can sustain you, but support becomes harder to feel when possessions occupy the room needed for a peaceful life of your own.
text: Feeling at home begins here with useful things and care visible in everyday life. The Empress in the physical position of Muladhara describes creating this tangible comfort. The Devil in energy tests your footing through attachment to possession: more supplies and ready conveniences seem to promise greater reliability. The Hermit in emotions seeks considered simplicity, room to hear yourself and a feeling that what you have chosen is enough. What you acquire may therefore bring pleasure while taking away the quiet that inspired you to make a home together.

Imagine having a separate gadget for every kitchen task. You carefully put everything in its place, yet making a simple dinner means moving several objects first. **Having enough feels freer when it leaves room for your life.** Sometimes a familiar knife and an empty worktop are sufficient. Preparing something simple together in peace can reveal which conveniences actually serve you and which have long been demanding care themselves.

The difficulty is seeking relief through another organiser or device. It promises order but adds something else to what already holds your attention. The wish to step away from the bustle grows, while discussing possessions becomes uncomfortable because each contains so much effort. Support becomes clearer when you can recognise the value of care without preserving all its material traces.
